rules.title: An autocomplete attribute holds only tokens the HTML standard defines (email, given-name, new-password…).
Never remove the focus outline without drawing a visible replacement for keyboard focus.
An input error is shown in text next to the field, tied to it with aria-describedby, and says how to fix it.
The html element names the language of the page in a non-empty lang attribute.
Every img and area element has an alt attribute; a decorative image has alt="".
Every form field has a programmatic label (label element, aria-label or aria-labelledby); a placeholder is not a label.
A click handler belongs on a button or link; a static element with one also needs a role, tabindex and a key handler.
Every HTML document has a title element that says what the page is about.
No element has a tabindex greater than 0; focus order follows the source order.
The viewport never disables zoom (no user-scalable=no, no maximum-scale below 2).
Two-way binding is written [(prop)], brackets outside; ([prop]) silently binds an event named [prop] instead.
Derive state with computed() (or linkedSignal()); never copy one signal into another inside effect().
Templates use the built-in @if, @for and @switch blocks, not the ngIf, ngFor and ngSwitch directives deprecated in v20.
An @for block tracks a stable unique field of the item (track item.id), not the item object itself.
Static images in Angular templates use NgOptimizedImage (ngSrc with width and height, or fill), not a plain src.
DomSanitizer bypassSecurityTrust calls never receive user or server data; each one is a reviewed exception.
A routerLinkActive link also sets ariaCurrentWhenActive, so the current page is announced, not only styled.
Code that runs on the server never touches window, document, navigator or localStorage directly; use DI or afterNextRender.
Table rows in Angular templates sit inside an explicit tbody (or thead/tfoot); the browser inserts one and hydration fails.
Give client:only the framework of the component (client:only="react"), and a fallback slot for the space it fills.
Put client: directives only on UI framework components imported into the .astro file, never on Astro components.
Never give a secret the PUBLIC_ prefix; in Astro those variables are built into client code. Declare secrets in astro:env as server secrets.
Astro script tags carry no attribute but src so they are bundled; is:inline only on purpose, data- instead of define:vars.
A server island (server:defer) has slot="fallback" content of the same size, and receives only small serializable props.
Render framework components without a client directive unless they need interactivity, and pick the latest directive that works.
Animations and transitions change transform and opacity, not layout properties such as width, height, top, left or margin.
In a bundled project, url() to images and fonts is a relative path or alias the bundler resolves, not a hard-coded root or public/ path.
Before using a newer CSS feature, check its Baseline status against the project's browser targets and plan the fallback.
Query containers use container-type inline-size; size is only for elements that get their height from elsewhere.
Colours and spacing come from the project's tokens (custom properties or variables); a literal that has a token, or repeats, is a finding.
Space the children of a flex or grid container with gap, not with margins on the children and last-child exceptions.
With a generated icon set, CSS uses its icon classes or mixin, never a url() hard-coded to an icon file.
A project that uses light-dark() declares color-scheme (light dark) on :root or in a meta tag, or the dark values never apply.
CSS that is not Baseline yet (anchor positioning) or only just became Baseline (scroll-driven animations) sits in @supports with a fallback.
Sites that run or may run right to left use logical properties (margin-inline-start, inset-inline-end), not left and right.
In native CSS nesting, never build class names from "&" plus a suffix (&__title); write the full selector.
Boxes that hold text do not combine a fixed height with hidden overflow; use min-height so enlarged or spaced text is not clipped.
Page and component layout uses grid or flexbox; float is only for wrapping text around media, and clearfix hacks are gone.
Style elements by class, not by id; an id selector outweighs any number of classes and makes the rule hard to override.
!important appears only in utility classes, user-preference overrides and third-party overrides, never to win a specificity fight.
Offsets and spacing use the project's spacing scale or come from layout; hand-tuned one-off values such as top -7px are a finding.
No hand-written vendor prefixes for features browsers support unprefixed (border-radius, transitions, transforms, flexbox, gradients).
Anything that moves, blinks or scrolls on its own for more than five seconds (carousels, marquees, background video) can be paused.
Non-essential motion (entrance animations, parallax, smooth scrolling) respects prefers-reduced-motion.
Font sizes and spacing use the project's px-to-rem helper (its rem function), not raw px.
Font sizes are written in rem (or em), never px, in projects without a rem helper; with one, css/rem-helper applies.
line-height is a unitless number (for example 1.5), never px, em or a percentage, so it scales with each element's font size.
z-index values come from a named scale (custom properties or Sass variables), not ad hoc numbers such as 999 or 9999.
Every button states its type (button, submit or reset); the default is submit.
Validation attributes match the input type (pattern and maxlength on text-like types, min, max and step on number and date types).
Every HTML document starts with <!doctype html> so the browser renders it in standards mode.
Fields sit in a form that is handled on its submit event with a submit button, so Enter, autofill and native validation work.
When the project has an icon set (sprite, icon classes or an Icon component), markup uses it, never a hard-coded path to an icon file.
An input for an email address, phone number or URL uses type email, tel or url, not text.
Codes made of digits (postal codes, card numbers, one-time codes, PINs) use type text with inputmode numeric, not type number.
Password fields say current-password (sign-in) or new-password (sign-up, change) in autocomplete, and never use autocomplete off.
Every picture element ends with an img that has src, alt, width and height; source elements alone render nothing.
Icons use the project's generated icon classes (its icon classes), not separate SVG image files.
A required single-choice select starts with an empty placeholder option (value=""), so the required check can fail.
In a bundled project, images, fonts and media in component markup are imported or use the base-path helper, not hard-coded root paths.
Never insert content with document.write; create elements or load scripts with the DOM.
Test for the feature you need (in, CSS.supports, matchMedia), not the browser name in navigator.userAgent.
After fetch, check response.ok (or the status) before reading the body; fetch does not reject on 404 or 500.
Listeners, timers and observers a view starts are removed when it goes away; one AbortController signal can end them all.
A catch block never swallows an error silently; handle it, report it, or say in a comment why it is safe to ignore.
Never run strings as code - no eval, new Function, or a string as the first argument of setTimeout or setInterval.
Every promise is awaited, returned or given a .catch(); an async call is never left floating.
Attach event handlers from script with addEventListener, not with onclick="..." attributes in HTML.
Declare variables with const, or let when they are reassigned; never with var.
Mark touchstart, touchmove and wheel listeners { passive true } unless the handler really calls preventDefault().
Compare with === and !==; loose == and != convert types first (x == null as a deliberate null-or-undefined test is the exception).
Throw and reject with Error objects (or subclasses), never with strings or plain objects.
Await params and searchParams in App Router pages, layouts and generateMetadata; Next.js 16 removed synchronous access.
A next/image with fill (or sized by CSS) sets sizes, so the browser does not download a viewport-wide file for a small slot.
A Client Component is never an async function; fetch in a Server Component parent or read a promise with use().
Never give a secret the NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix; those values are copied into the JavaScript every visitor downloads.
Call redirect(), notFound() and their kin outside try blocks; they work by throwing, and a catch swallows them.
Every Server Action checks who is calling and what they may change, validates its input and returns only what the UI needs.
Keep App Router pages and layouts Server Components; put 'use client' on the small interactive component they render.
Load web fonts with next/font (google or local), not a link or @import to the Google Fonts stylesheet.
In a Next.js app, render images with next/image instead of a plain img element (a picture element with its own sources is fine).
A composable that wraps useAsyncData passes an explicit, unique key built from its inputs.
Call useFetch and useAsyncData only in setup, plugins or composables; in event handlers use $fetch.
Load a page's initial data with useFetch or useAsyncData, not a bare $fetch at the top of script setup.
Never touch window, document, localStorage or navigator at the top of script setup; it also runs on the server.
Never create ref() or reactive() state at module scope in a Nuxt app; use useState or a Pinia store.
Secrets live in the top level of runtimeConfig, never under runtimeConfig.public, which every page sends to the browser.
The app renders NuxtRouteAnnouncer (in app.vue or a layout) so client-side page changes are announced.
App code reads configuration with useRuntimeConfig() and tests the side with import.meta.client, not process.env or process.client.
Every @font-face and Google Fonts URL sets font-display (swap or optional) so text is visible while the font loads.
The fallback font is adjusted to the web font's metrics (size-adjust and overrides) so the swap does not shift the layout.
Fonts are self-hosted, or the font CDN's file origin (fonts.gstatic.com) is preconnected with crossorigin.
A font preload has crossorigin (and type font/woff2); without it the preload is wasted and the font is fetched twice.
Web fonts are served as WOFF2; TTF, OTF, EOT and plain WOFF files are dead weight for current browsers.
Animations longer than a small icon are shipped as a muted, looping MP4 or WebM video, not as a GIF over 100 KiB.
Every img has width and height attributes (or a CSS aspect ratio) so the browser reserves its space.
Photos and large raster images are served as AVIF or WebP at the size they are shown, not as large JPEG or PNG files.
An image file in the source stays under the image budget (250 KB by default); larger ones are resized or re-encoded.
The image that is likely the LCP element loads eagerly with fetchpriority high; it is never lazy-loaded.
A script in the head loads with defer, async or type="module", never as a plain blocking script.
A srcset with width descriptors (400w, 800w) comes with a sizes attribute that matches the image's displayed width.
A list item's key comes from the data (an id), not from the array index.
Values computed from props or state are calculated during render, not copied into state by an effect.
Components are declared at module level, never inside another component's body.
A full-height layout uses 100dvh (or svh) instead of 100vh, which is taller than the visible area on mobile.
No layout box gets a fixed width wider than 320 CSS px; cap it with max-width or min(100%, …) so the page reflows on narrow screens.
Nothing is revealed on hover alone; content and controls shown on hover also show on keyboard focus and are reachable on touch.
Text is never sized with viewport units alone (font-size 5vw); fluid type mixes in rem, as in clamp(1rem, 0.9rem + 1vw, 1.5rem).
The page works in portrait and landscape; it never locks the orientation or asks people to rotate unless one orientation is essential.
The page reads without sideways scrolling at 320 CSS px and 400% zoom; only tables, maps and similar may scroll both ways.
Every HTML document has <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">.
Values that change at run time (themes, dark mode, user settings) are CSS custom properties; Sass variables are for build-time constants.
Divide with math.div() in Sass; a slash between Sass values is becoming a list separator, as it is in CSS.
Extend only placeholder selectors (%name), or use a mixin; @extend of a real class copies selectors everywhere it appears.
Call Sass built-in functions through their module (map.get, math.div, string.index) after @use "sass:...", not as globals.
Load Sass files with @use and @forward, not @import, which is deprecated and will be removed in Dart Sass 3.
Adjust colours with color.scale or color.adjust (and read channels with color.channel), not darken, lighten, fade-out and the like.
Compile Sass with Dart Sass (the sass or sass-embedded package), never node-sass, which is deprecated LibSass.
Sizes are converted with the project's px-to-rem function, never by dividing by a hard-coded base by hand.
An effect that fetches into state returns a cleanup that ignores or aborts stale responses.
A Redux Toolkit or Immer reducer either mutates the draft or returns a new state, never both; no arrow that returns a mutation.
After a mutation succeeds, invalidate or update every cached query it changed, so lists and details show the new data.
Data fetched from a server lives in the framework's loader or a server-state cache, not copied into a client store.
State and getters taken out of a Pinia store go through storeToRefs(); plain destructuring freezes them at their first value.
The QueryClient is created once - in useState(() => new QueryClient()) or a module helper - never in a component's render.
A component that reads a query (TanStack Query, SWR) also reads its error and shows it; it never renders only data.
A TanStack Query key holds every variable its query function reads, so a new id fetches new data instead of showing the old.
TanStack Query 5 hooks take one options object; the v4 positional form useQuery(key, fn) and useMutation(fn) no longer works.
New and maintained Redux code uses Redux Toolkit's configureStore and createSlice, not the legacy createStore.
A store selector returns existing values, not a new object or array on every call; pick fields one by one or use useShallow or shallowEqual.
Server data comes from the framework loader or a server-state library, not fetch plus useState and loading flags in each component.
State a person would share, bookmark or restore with Back (filters, sort, page, selected tab, search) lives in the URL.
A value computed from state is a $derived, not a $state that an $effect keeps in sync.
An each block whose items hold state (inputs, bindings, components, transitions) is keyed by a unique id, never by the index.
Read page, navigating and updated from $app/state, not the $app/stores module that SvelteKit 3 removed.
A SvelteKit form posts to a form action (method and action) and is enhanced with use:enhance, not handled only by onsubmit.
A load function starts independent requests together and awaits parent() only after them, so data does not load in a chain.
Every SvelteKit page sets its own descriptive title in svelte:head, or its layout renders a title from page data.
Server code of a SvelteKit app never keeps per-request data in module-level variables; the module is shared by every user.
New Svelte 5 code uses runes and the new syntax, not export let, $:, on:event, slot or svelte:component.
A top-level value computed from props is a $derived; a plain let or const keeps only the first value.
Listen to window and document events with svelte:window and svelte:document, not addEventListener in $effect or onMount.
Remove repeated class lists with a component, a loop or a partial; keep @apply for small cases and third-party markup.
One element never carries two utilities that set the same property under the same variant (p-2 p-4, flex grid).
Content or controls revealed with hover: are also revealed on focus (focus-within:, group-focus-within:), never on hover alone.
Decorative Tailwind animations (animate-bounce, animate-ping, animate-pulse) run under motion-safe: or stop under motion-reduce:.
Write every Tailwind class as a complete string; never build one from fragments such as bg-${color}-500.
Do not run Tailwind CSS 4 through Sass, Less or Stylus; use plain CSS with native nesting and variables.
The only text of a button or link is never hidden with hidden; use sr-only (with md:not-sr-only to show it on wider screens).
An arbitrary value used again and again (bg-[#0a7a3e], p-[18px]) becomes a theme variable in @theme with its own utility.
In Tailwind CSS 4, load Tailwind with @import "tailwindcss" and a legacy JS config with @config; @tailwind directives do nothing.
A Vite project's tsconfig sets isolatedModules or verbatimModuleSyntax, so code the bundler compiles file by file type-checks the same way.
A TypeScript 6 or 7 tsconfig uses no option deprecated in 6.0 and removed in 7.0 (baseUrl, moduleResolution node, target es5).
Type values with a real type or unknown (then narrow), never any.
Silence a type error with @ts-expect-error and a reason, never @ts-ignore or @ts-nocheck.
TypeScript runs with strict on; no config turns strict or one of its checks (strictNullChecks, noImplicitAny...) off.
Data from outside the program (fetch, JSON.parse, storage) is validated at run time, not given a type with as or an annotation.
A computed getter only derives a value - no async work, no requests and no changes to other state.
Declare props with their types (an object with type, or a TypeScript type), not as a bare array of names.
Navigate with RouterLink or NuxtLink, not a button whose click handler only calls router.push or navigateTo.
Name components with two or more words (TodoItem, not Item); App, pages and layouts are exempt.
A v-for key comes from the item's data, not from the loop index, when the list can change.
A component never changes its props (or objects and arrays inside them); it emits an event or keeps a local copy.
Never destructure or reassign a reactive() object; use toRefs, a ref, or change its properties.
Never put v-if and v-for on the same element; filter in a computed list or move v-if to a wrapper.
In script code, read and compare a ref or computed through .value; the ref object itself is always truthy.
Every v-for gives its items a :key from the data; on a template v-for the key goes on the template tag.
id references (for, aria-labelledby, aria-describedby, aria-controls) point at an element in the same DOM tree, not across a shadow root.
A custom element constructor never reads or adds attributes or children; do that in connectedCallback.
A custom form control is form-associated (formAssociated and attachInternals) and reports its value and validity to the form.
Shadow styles that give :host a display also add :host([hidden]) { display none }, or the hidden attribute stops working.
In JavaScript, a Lit reactive property is never also declared as a class field; the field hides Lit's accessor and updates stop.
A Lit reactive array is replaced, not mutated in place (push, splice, sort), unless requestUpdate() follows.
Lit's unsafeHTML, unsafeSVG and unsafeStatic only receive strings the developer wrote or sanitized, never data.
Build autonomous custom elements that wrap a native element; do not extend built-ins with is=, which Safari does not support.
A custom element name is lowercase, starts with a letter, contains a hyphen and is not a reserved name, or define() throws.
